    Notes on Linear algebra

    skew symmetric

    Edit

    For a real \(m\times m\) matrix \(A\): \(\|A\|_{\rm op}=\max_{|x|=1}|Ax|\) is the operator norm; \(\|A\|_{\rm HS}^2=\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}^2=\operatorname{tr}(A^tA)\) is the Hilbert-Schmidt norm. The matrix \(A^tA\) is symmetric and positive semidefinite, so it has an orthonormal eigenbasis with eigenvalues \(\mu_1\ge\mu_2\ge\dots\ge\mu_m\ge0\). Then

    \[\|A\|_{\rm op}^2=\max_{|x|=1}\langle A^tAx,x\rangle=\mu_1,\qquad \|A\|_{\rm HS}^2=\operatorname{tr}(A^tA)=\mu_1+\dots+\mu_m .\]

    For a general matrix this only gives \(\|A\|_{\rm op}^2\le\|A\|_{\rm HS}^2\). Equality is possible, for example when \(A\) has rank one. Skew-symmetry improves the constant to \(\tfrac12\).

    Exercise
    Edit

    Suppose \(A\) is a real skew-symmetric matrix. Then

    \[\|A\|_{\rm op}^2\le \tfrac12\|A\|_{\rm HS}^2.\]

    Proof
    Edit

    The key fact: nonzero eigenvalues of \(A^tA\) have even multiplicity.

    Let \(A^t=-A\). Then \(A^tA=-A^2\), which commutes with \(A\).

    Fix an eigenvalue \(\mu>0\) of \(A^tA\) and let \(E=\{x: A^tAx=\mu x\}\) be its eigenspace.

    \(A\) maps \(E\) into \(E\): If \(x\in E\), then \(A^tA(Ax)=A(A^tAx)=\mu\,Ax\), so \(Ax\in E\).

    On \(E\) we have \(A^2=-\mu\): This holds because \(A^2=-A^tA\). \(E\) has even dimension. Put \(J=\mu^{-1/2}A|_E\). By step 2, \(J:E\to E\) satisfies \(J^2=-I_E\). Taking determinants gives

    \[(\det J)^2=\det(-I_E)=(-1)^{\dim E}.\]

    The left side is a square of a real number, hence nonnegative, so \(\dim E\) is even. In other words, \(J\) is a complex structure on \(E\).

    So the largest eigenvalue \(\mu_1=\|A\|_{\rm op}^2\) appears at least twice in the list \(\mu_1,\dots,\mu_m\) (when \(A\neq0\)). Hence

    \[\|A\|_{\rm HS}^2=\sum_k\mu_k\ \ge\ 2\mu_1=2\|A\|_{\rm op}^2 .\]

    A hands-on version of the same argument. Choose a unit vector \(v\) with \(|Av|=\|A\|_{\rm op}=:\lambda>0\). Then \(v\) is a top eigenvector of \(A^tA\), so \(A^2v=-\lambda^2v\). Put \(w=Av/\lambda\). Then:

    \(|w|=1\); \(\langle v,w\rangle=\lambda^{-1}\langle v,Av\rangle=0\), because \(\langle v,Av\rangle=\langle A^tv,v\rangle=-\langle Av,v\rangle\); \(Aw=A^2v/\lambda=-\lambda v\), so \(|Aw|=\lambda\).

    Complete \(v,w\) to an orthonormal basis \(\{e_i\}\). Since \(\|A\|_{\rm HS}^2=\sum_i|Ae_i|^2\) for any orthonormal basis,

    \[\|A\|_{\rm HS}^2\ \ge\ |Av|^2+|Aw|^2=2\lambda^2 .\]
